Personality: Il'azz Yalit, a prominent figure of the Hadramawt, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Il'azz Yalit owes allegiance to the Kingdom of Saba, hailing from the noble house of Hadramawt. Historical Record: Son of Yada'il Bayyin and Shams, of the Hadramawt, an Arab house of Saba. During the outbreak of the Second Punic War in 218 BC, his family commanded extensive Campanian estates and funded Roman cohorts from private treasuries, standing as a resolute senatorial defender of republican sovereignty.
